summary: Midday tenant-fanout blindspot causing ephemeral GPU thinness and autoscaler under-allocation
description:
Issue summary:
During a midday traffic wave (approx 11:45-12:15 UTC) VectorCart observed sustained p99 latency increase and dropped throughput on their dedicated pool. Symptoms looked like GPU scarcity even though dashboard showed spare capacity. The customer reports failed requests and timeouts for batched chat routes.

Impact:
- VectorCart dedicated pool (dedicated, us-east) experienced 25-40% throughput degradation for 30 minutes.
- Visible error spikes (5xx) and increased retry traffic.
- Customer SLA risk: interfering with checkout flows.

Environment:
- Product mode: dedicated capacity (reservation id: reserved-vec-11)
- Region: us-east
- Models: open-llama-7b pinned v2026-02-05
- Routes: /v1/chat (batched, short-streams mix)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer load pattern: large number of concurrent short chatlets (~150-250 concurrent connections) with moderate token rates, many short-lived keepalives.
2) System observed a sudden fanout of small, bursty streams to the reserved pool.
3) Autoscaler did not allocate extra ephemeral GPUs; allocator reported free slots but attach latency increased and some slots remained unusable (appeared as "thin").
4) Result: request queueing, elevated p99 latency, and intermittent 5xx failures.

Logs and artifacts:
- Dashboard: /dashboards/vec/reserved-pool-2026-03-10 (snapshot attached in ticket)
- Correlation id examples: vec-req-1982, vec-req-1997
- Sidecar logs: sidecar-attach-timeout observed at 2026-03-10T11:52:04Z
- Allocator traces: nvlink-attach-wait samples and slot-marked-unavailable events
comments: 2026-03-10 12:05 - Anika Patel: Initial triage - flagged to SRE oncall and escalated to Eng. Customer reported retries causing checkout delays. Asked for immediate mitigation (rate-shaping suggestion).

2026-03-10 13:12 - Diego Morales: Observed attach latency spike on reserved-vec-11. Free slot count reported inconsistent between allocator and attach path — hypothesis: slot state flap (MARKED_FREE but not attachable). Kicked off allocator debug logs collection.
2026-03-11 09:40 - SRE (Marta Kim): Correlated with autoscaler telemetry drop between 11:40-11:55. Autoscaler decision window had low visibility for many short streams (fanout blindspot).

2026-03-12 15:22 - Eng (Ravi Singh): Found prefetched KV cache growth causing slot reservation contention; sidecar backpressure causing ephemeral slots to be flagged but not usable. Preparing patch to make allocator treat prefetched-only slots differently.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Fanout blindspot - a high count of very short-lived streams falls below autoscaler's per-connection sampling window; autoscaler underestimates demand and does not request ephemeral GPUs quickly enough.

Hypothesis 2: Slot thinness - allocator state machine allowed slots to be in 'soft-free' state (free for accounting) while sidecar attach handshake was still in flight, creating a thin pool of attachable GPUs.

Finding: At 11:50 UTC 2026-03-10 we saw ~220 short connections causing a transient spike in sidecar attach attempts; allocator reported 12 free slots but 7 of them were in 'attach-in-progress' for >6s which the attach path treated as unavailable. This mismatch produced the illusion of spare capacity while actual attach concurrency was saturated.
Reproduction: We replayed a scaled-down client pattern in staging and reproduced attach-latency + queueing when mixing many short-lived streams with a few long-lived batched requests.
root_cause: Race between allocator accounting and attach handshake under high short-stream fanout. Autoscaler sampling window missed the short-lived fanout, and allocator marked slots as free while attach handshakes were saturating attach threads, resulting in effective GPU thinness despite measured free capacity.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporary rate-shaping guidance provided to customer and provisioned an emergency ephemeral buffer of 4 additional GPUs to the reserved pool for 2 hours. Engineering deployed a low-risk allocator patch to treat 'attach-in-progress' slots as unavailable for accounting (rollout to prod-us-east at 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC).
resolution_notes: Workaround: VectorCart applied short-term client-side jitter and connection keepalive tuning to reduce simultaneous attach pressure.
Patch: Allocator now excludes 'attach-in-progress' slots from free count; guarding logic added to reduce slot-thinness windows.
Deployment: Canaryed in us-east with 10% traffic for 2 hours then full rollout. No regression observed in p50/p99 post-rollout.
Monitoring: Added a new alert "Attach thread saturation" and dashboard panel to visualize attach-in-progress vs attachable-slots.
Follow-up: Longer-term autoscaler change to include short-stream sampling heuristic (ENG-1219).
follow_up_actions: SRE-428: Add dashboard and alert for Attach thread saturation and slot-state mismatch
CS-77: Customer-facing postmortem and recommended client tuning guide to distribute short-stream fanout
